title: Work that is not Done when the Sprint ends: what happens to it, how it is reported, and the Definition of Done

The company, the product, the team and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the Scrum Master for a fictional team building a payments feature for Quayside Bank's app. The Sprint ends in two days and two items are not Done.
handover: Definition of Done: code reviewed, automated tests passing, security scan clean, deployed to staging.
Item A is coded but its security scan has two high findings; item B is half built.
howItWorks: The board shows the Sprint's commitments, the work, the impediments, the people's support and the Scrum events.
Move on a day at a time. A decision comes to you at each Daily Scrum; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

board.label: Read the Sprint Backlog
board.available: not busy and phase == "run" and isNull(boardAt)
board.why: Done, or finish what you are doing first.

effects.finding: Item A: coded and tested, security scan failing. Item B: half built. Three items Done.

pressure.label: Talk to the stakeholder lead
pressure.available: not busy and phase == "run" and isNull(pressureAt)
pressure.why: Done, or finish what you are doing first.

effects.finding: She wants to tell the bank's board that all five items are complete.

options.label: Undone items returned to the Product Backlog, only Done work presented, and the Definition of Done kept with earlier scans

then.log: Day 10: one of the findings is exploited in production within a week; payments are paused.
Day 11: the board announces item B to customers; it is not built.
Day 11: the next Sprint's Increment ships an unscanned library with a known flaw.

choices.label: Item A does not meet the Definition of Done, so it is not part of the Increment; it returns to the Product Backlog for the Product Owner to order

effects.log: Item A goes back to the Product Backlog.

choices.feedback: Work that does not meet the Definition of Done cannot be released or presented as Done; it returns to the Product Backlog.

choices.label: Extend the Sprint by three days to finish it
choices.feedback: Sprints have a fixed length; extending one hides the problem and breaks the cadence.

choices.label: Release item A with a note to fix the findings next Sprint
choices.feedback: Two high security findings reach production in a banking app.

presentPrompt.title: Five items or three?
presentPrompt.context: The stakeholder lead wants to report five complete.

choices.label: Present the three Done items as the Increment and explain items A and B and where they are in the backlog

effects.log: Stakeholders see three Done and two in progress.

choices.feedback: Presenting undone work as Done destroys the transparency inspection relies on.

choices.label: Report 'most of the scope delivered'
choices.feedback: Not false, but stakeholders cannot tell what is usable.

choices.label: Report all five items as complete
choices.feedback: The board plans around features that do not exist.

doneDefPrompt.title: Should the Definition of Done loosen?
doneDefPrompt.context: A developer suggests dropping the security scan from the Definition of Done.

choices.label: Keep the security scan in the Definition of Done and plan to run scans earlier in the Sprint so findings surface sooner

effects.log: Scans move earlier; the Definition stays.

choices.feedback: The Definition of Done sets the quality the Increment must meet; the team improves its work to meet it, not the other way round.

choices.label: Allow the scan to be waived when time is short
choices.feedback: A Definition of Done that can be waived stops meaning Done.

choices.label: Remove the security scan from the Definition of Done
choices.feedback: Every future Increment can ship unscanned code.

reflection.question: Write the Sprint notes on what was Done and what was not.

parts.label: The Increment
parts.criteria: Three items Done; A and B back in the Product Backlog.
parts.modelAnswer: Three items met the Definition of Done. Item A failed its security scan and item B was half built; both returned to the Product Backlog.

parts.label: Quality
parts.criteria: Definition of Done kept; scans earlier.
parts.modelAnswer: We kept the security scan in the Definition of Done and will run scans earlier in the Sprint.

undoneHarm.label: A vulnerability exploited
undoneHarm.narrative: Releasing undone work shipped an exploitable flaw.

presentHarm.label: A public promise broken
presentHarm.narrative: Reporting undone work as Done led to a false announcement.

doneDefHarm.label: Unscanned code shipped
doneDefHarm.narrative: Dropping the scan let a known flaw into the next Increment.

target.label: Done means Done
target.when: closed and (undone == "backlog") and (present == "onlyDone") and (doneDef == "keepDod") and record == "honest" and missCount <= undoneShown and minSupport >= trustTarget
target.narrative: Stakeholders can trust what the team calls Done, and quality holds.

expertPath.text: Read the Sprint Backlog and the Definition of Done first.
Return undone work to the Product Backlog.
Present only what meets the Definition of Done.
Keep the Definition of Done and scan earlier.

undoneHarm.headline: Done means Done
undoneHarm.body: Undone work returns to the Product Backlog.

doneDefHarm.headline: Raise quality, don't lower Done
doneDefHarm.body: Keep the Definition; improve the work.

target.headline: Good: done means Done
target.body: Undone work handled, reported and prevented honestly.

partly.headline: Done, with gaps
partly.body: Nothing was harmed, but a decision was only partly right, or the record left something out. The criteria say which.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: The record was not written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Work that does not meet the Definition of Done is not part of the Increment and cannot be released or presented as Done; it returns to the Product Backlog. Sprints are not extended to finish it. The team improves how it meets the Definition of Done rather than weakening it.
